newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama calls first ever Eurobond issue a success.
newsitem.headline: Panama calls first ever Eurobond issue a success.

text.p: Panama's Minister of Planning and Economic Policy Guillermo Chapman said Tuesday the government's first-ever Eurobond issue was successful.
"I'm positive about our achieving our main goal with this Eurobond transaction," Chapman told Reuters.

"We tapped the international markets successfully, not just for the (Panamanian) government but for banks and private enterprise. They needed long-term money at competitive rates and that has been achieved," he said.
The $500 million 7.875 percent five-year Eurobond issue was made on Feb 10.
BankBoston Corp was lead manager for the transaction which was priced to yield 175 basis points more than comparable U.S. Treasury notes.
The launch spread was the tightest spread for an inaugural public sector issue out of Latin America.

The funds will be used to help pay off the nation's external debt. Panama completed its Brady bond external debt restructuring package last year by issuing bonds in exchange for $3.5 billion of medium- and long-term commercial debt.
The decision to issue Eurobonds came close on the heels on rating assignments from both Moody's Investors Services and Standard & Poor's Corp.
Moody's assigned Panama Brady bonds a Ba1 rating, while S&P gave them a BB-plus. The ratings are among the highest in Latin America and were the first grading of the Central American nation's debt.
